header:
Date: 2027-09-28
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Lee (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood CSM), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (CedarPoint Head of Eng), Dr. Aaron Patel (CTO), Lena Ortiz (Security Lead), Samir Khan (DevOps)
Recording: Yes
Notes: Onboarding kickoff for CedarPoint Health - initial alignment on scope, security, trial plan, and technical integration.
summary: Kickoff to align on CedarPoint's onboarding to Redwood. Covered high-level goals (production inference for clinical NLP use cases), timeline for pilot, required security/compliance docs, networking (VPC) requirements, and initial benchmark plan. Action items assigned for pricing/SOW, trial workspace, benchmarks, and security artifacts. Customer expressed interest in dedicated capacity for predictable latency once pilot succeeds; security questions and data residency discussed.
topics: Introductions; Use cases and success criteria; Architecture options (hosted vs dedicated vs private); Security and compliance (SOC2, SSO, KMS); Network/VPC and deployment steps; Benchmarks and metrics (latency, throughput, cost); Trial plan and timeline; Next steps and owners.
transcript:
00:00 Speaker 1 (Samantha): Hi everyone, thanks for joining, this is Samantha from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, with Diego and Ethan from our team. Uh, quick roll call?
00:12 Speaker 2 (Maya): Hey Samantha, Maya here. Aaron, Lena, Samir are on too.
00:20 Speaker 1 (Samantha): Awesome, thanks. Goal for today is a quick alignment on scope and to capture action items for the pilot. Ethan, do you want to run through the tech agenda?
00:30 Speaker 3 (Ethan): Yeah sure, real quick. We'll cover model access (text gen, embeddings), deployment modes \u2014 hosted API, dedicated pools, private VPC \u2014 then networking, security, and a baseline benchmark plan. Apologies if I mis-say any product names, sometimes the auto transcriber makes Redwood names weird.
00:48 Speaker 4 (Dr. Aaron): That's fine. For context, CedarPoint's main goal is to run clinical note summarization and some QA search embeddings across patient data. We need sub-second p95 for summaries in production.
01:05 Speaker 3 (Ethan): Understood. Sub-second p95 is realistic on smaller seq lengths but depends on model size, batching, and whether you go hosted or dedicated. Dedicated gives more consistent latency but has cost/commit implications.
01:20 Speaker 2 (Diego): We typically suggest starting hosted for speed to value, run a short pilot, then move to dedicated if you need capacity guarantees. For clinical data you mentioned, the private VPC option is available for regulated workloads.
01:35 Speaker 5 (Lena): On security: SOC2 is a must, we also need audit logs, encryption across rest and in-transit, KMS integration. Can you support customer-managed keys or HSM?
01:48 Speaker 3 (Ethan): Yes, Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM for on-prem or VPC deployments. We'll share our security pack with the SOC2 report \u2014 note there may be redactions but full auditor access is possible with an NDA.
02:05 Speaker 4 (Dr. Aaron): Great. Also need SSO (SAML/Okta) and RBAC for team roles. And data residency \u2014 some data must stay in us-east-1.
02:20 Speaker 1 (Samantha): We support SAML and Okta integrations, and Redwood can pin region for deployments. We'll include region notes in the SOW.
02:32 Speaker 6 (Samir): On the infra side, we'll need a VPC peering or PrivateLink style connectivity. Firewall rules, egress restrictions, that sort of thing. Do you have an IaC template?
02:45 Speaker 3 (Ethan): Yep, we'll share Terraform templates for VPC peering and example security groups. Also, if you go dedicated we can do private endpoints in your VPC.
03:00 Speaker 2 (Diego): For the pilot, proposed scope: 3 weeks, small dataset, run 5000 summarization requests and embedding index of ~200k docs to validate throughput and quality. Benchmark script will capture p50/p95 latency and token cost.
03:20 Speaker 4 (Dr. Aaron): That sounds about right. On quality, we want to measure ROUGE and some human evals for hallucination rate \u2014 can Redwood help with eval tooling?
03:33 Speaker 3 (Ethan): Yes, Redwood Optimize has evaluation hooks \u2014 we can help set up prompt sets and regression alerts. If you want, Ethan will own running the first evals with your prompts.
03:45 Speaker 5 (Lena): Also, we need to know retention: how long do you keep logs? Can we set retention and purge policies?
03:55 Speaker 2 (Diego): Default telemetry retention is 90 days, but for enterprise we can configure longer retention or special export pipelines. We'll include options in the SOW.
04:10 Speaker 1 (Samantha): I'd like to talk pricing model quickly \u2014 hosted is usage-based per token, dedicated is a reserved capacity model. Customer: do you have a rough budget or prefer to evaluate and then we propose?
04:25 Speaker 4 (Dr. Aaron): We have a preliminary budget for pilot but need a pricing sheet to present to procurement. Also procurement will ask about SLAs and support tiers.
04:35 Speaker 1 (Samantha): We'll send a pricing sheet and an example SOW that includes SLA targets for dedicated.
04:42 Speaker 6 (Samir): One technical question: you mentioned KV cache and quantization. How mature are those features for clinical models?
04:50 Speaker 3 (Ethan): KV cache is standard for seq generation to reduce repeated compute, and we support quantized model variants for cost. For clinical accuracy, quantization can sometimes affect quality, so we recommend A/B testing. We'll run both float16 and int8 runs in the benchmarks.
05:10 Speaker 5 (Lena): Do you support private model upload or bring-your-own-model? We have a fine-tuned model with PHI pre-processing constraints.
05:20 Speaker 3 (Ethan): Yes, Private deployment supports BYOM and air-gapped installs. For hosted, we can host private models in a dedicated pool within your VPC. We'll coordinate E2E security.
05:35 Speaker 2 (Diego): I'll set up access to a trial workspace this week and invite the CedarPoint engineering group. That will include API keys scoped to a sandbox project.
05:44 Speaker 4 (Dr. Aaron): Perfect. Timeline: can we aim to start pilot the week of Oct 4?
05:52 Speaker 1 (Samantha): Yes, that's feasible. Diego will provision workspace by Sep 30, Ethan will start benchmarks first week of Oct, SOW finalized by Oct 2.
06:03 Speaker 6 (Samir): On networking, I'll send a VPC diagram and the list of ports we can open.
06:10 Speaker 5 (Lena): I'll compile compliance questions and auditors.
06:14 Speaker 1 (Samantha): Great. Any blockers?
06:18 Speaker 4 (Dr. Aaron): Just procurement signoff \u2014 we need the pricing and SLA to review.
06:24 Speaker 2 (Diego): We'll include a procurement appendix and contact for enterprise sales.
06:30 Speaker 3 (Ethan): Quick note \u2014 we sometimes see transcription/term errors on these calls, e.g., folks say "KV cache" and the auto transcriber spits out different words; ignore small mis-terms.
06:40 Speaker 1 (Samantha): Ok final recap of next steps: SOW/pricing from Samantha, trial workspace from Diego, baselines from Ethan, VPC diagram from Samir, compliance qs from Lena. Anyone want to add?
06:55 Speaker 2 (Diego): I'll also share our onboarding checklist and playbook.
07:05 Speaker 4 (Dr. Aaron): No, that covers it. Thanks everyone.
07:10 Speaker 1 (Samantha): Thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the tech deep-dive and send the docs. Meeting ends.
